newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan's Tomen to build fertiliser plant in Vietnam.
newsitem.headline: Japan's Tomen to build fertiliser plant in Vietnam.

text.p: Japan's Tomen Corp said on Wednesday that it had agreed with a Vietnamese state company to construct a phosphatic fertiliser plant in Vietnam.

The trade house said it would invest nearly 20 billion yen to build the plant near Hanoi with the Vietnam National Chemical Corporation. It said the plant would have the capacity to produce 330,000 tonnes of fertiliser a year.

Vietnam consumes about a million tonnes of phosphatic fertiliser annually and currently depends on imports. "But they have ample reserves of phosphate rock to make the fertiliser. We'd like to take advantage of it," a Tomen spokesman said.

"We'd like to start construction next April and actual operations as early as 2000," the Tomen spokesman said, adding the fertiliser would be sold in Vietnam. -- Tokyo Commodities Desk +81-3-3432-7391
